assertion_analysis.fails_if: Restoring the module-level _publish_exec_identity() call at import makes the file exist again; proven red by logs/negative-control.log.
Removing _retire_exec_identity() from _NodeDispatchClaim.release leaves the file behind after the subprocess exits.
Retiring on the refusal path without the held counter check unlinks the identity of the still-held first claim, so :95 reddens; not retiring at release fails :97.
Dropping exec_identity from the claim record raises KeyError at :104; breaking the reclaim decision fails :109-111. Not a regression guard for this change, since it passes at base too.
A sweep that keeps every file, or removes the live pid's file, or prints nothing, fails these four assertions; the sweep does not exist at base, so it is red there.
A sweep that unlinks regardless of apply removes the file and fails :147.
A sweep that accepts a live pid without comparing start time against the file's mtime keeps the file and fails :160.

assertion_independence: No added assertion compares a value the test supplied against the code's own echo of it. The nearest is tests/test_an_execution_identity_is_published_with_its_claim.py:104, where both sides derive from the module token _EXEC_IDENTITY; it still reddens if the claim record omits exec_identity, but it cannot detect a wrong token on both sides, so the guard there is the key's presence rather than its value.
call_sites: reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:738 (_claim_holder_is_alive reads the identity file for the reclaim decision)
reckon/crew/runs.py:4692 (process_liveness re-export the sweep does not use)

findings.text: non-blocking: _execution_is_live re-implements process_alive (owner reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:12, re-exported at reckon/crew/runs.py:4692) and drops its zombie rule at process_liveness.py:33-34, so a pid the kernel still lists as Z passes os.kill(pid, 0) and gets a start time and its identity file is kept, leaving the file of a process that has exited, exactly the case section 2's sweep is meant to remove; extend the owner rather than restating it.

non-blocking: _process_start_epoch re-parses the /proc/<pid>/stat field layout that reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:503-514 (_process_stat_fields, _process_start_time) already owns, making a third copy of the comm-parenthesis and field-19 knowledge; an epoch accessor on the owner would give the sweep what it needs without the copy.

non-blocking: the sweep writes 'removing identity file ...' to stderr for every entry it would remove even when apply=False, so a report pass states removals it did not make while tests/test_an_execution_identity_is_published_with_its_claim.py:146 treats the same report as a dry run; print a would-remove wording unless apply.

non-blocking: the landed change makes this pre-existing assertion fail at 90617f00b9, because an import no longer publishes an identity file; the file is outside this node's write fence, so the merged suite stays red until a paired node deletes the subprocess-import assertion at lines 41-51, which the coordinator must queue before promotion measures the merged head.

non-blocking: the plan's measure names all_debug for both arms, and the manifest records them run in the fleet allocation (job 1291586) instead; the gates took 13 s and 24 s so the result stands, but the named environment was not used and the deviation is unrecorded in the manifest.
